# Igusa, *A classification of spinors up to dimension twelve* (1970)

[I] J.-I. Igusa, *A classification of spinors up to dimension twelve*, Amer. J. Math. 92 (1970),
no. 4, 997–1028. Igusa works with algebraic groups over a universal domain; the statements here are
for the groups of `F`-points, `F` a field of characteristic zero (or `ℂ`, a subfield of `ℂ`, `ℚ`,
`K = ℚ(√-d)` where the paper uses them). The model is the Fock model of `WeilClasses.Spinor.Defs`:
`V_F = H¹(X, F)* × H¹(X, F)`, `S_F = ⋀• H¹(X, F)`, `m_{(θ, w)} = L_w + D_θ`, `Spin(V_F)` = Mathlib's
`spinGroup`, `ρ(g) v = g v g*`. All files were proved by prover SC (helper prefix `sc_`).

## `Sec2_4.lean`: [I, §2], the elements `s(λ)` (used in Remark 2.4.3 and §2.2)

* `igusa_sec2_mem`: `s(λ) = λ⁻¹ + (λ - λ⁻¹) a b ∈ Spin(V_F)` for a hyperbolic pair `a, b`.
* `igusa_sec2_rho`: `ρ(s(λ))` multiplies `a` by `λ²`, `b` by `λ⁻²` and fixes `{a, b}^⊥`.

Proved. `s(λ) = (a + b)(λ⁻¹ a + λ b)` is a product of two vectors of norm `1`, hence in `Spin`
(Tau Ceti's `ι_mul_ι_mem_spinGroup_of_norm_mul_norm_eq_one`), and acts by the product of the two
reflections (`spinToOrthogonal_eq_reflection_mul_reflection_of_coe_eq`); closed form of the action:
`sc_rho_igusaFactor_eq`.

## `Sec2_2.lean`: [I, Lemma 1] and [I, Lemma 2] with the remark after it (used in §2.2, Remark 2.2.3)

For even pure spinors `u₁, u₂` with `W₁ ∩ W₂ = 0` (`Wᵢ = ker m_{uᵢ}`):

* `igusa_lemma1_ker`: `Spin(V)_{ℓ₁,ℓ₂} → GL(W₁)` has kernel `{±1}`;
* `igusa_lemma1_range`: its image is `{A ∈ GL(W₁) : det A is a square}` (the form valid for
  `F`-points; Igusa's `≅ GL(W₁)` holds over quadratically closed fields);
* `igusa_lemma1_dual`: `ρ(g)` is an isometry (so acts on `W₂ ≅ W₁*` by the inverse transpose);
* `igusa_lemma1_sq`: `g u = c u ⇒ c² = det(ρ(g)|_{W₁})`;
* `igusa_lemma2_stab_odd` (`n ≥ 3` odd): the stabilizer of `w = a u₁ + b u₂` (`a, b ≠ 0`) is the
  pointwise stabilizer of `u₁, u₂`;
* `igusa_lemma2_stab_even` (`n ≥ 3` even): the pointwise stabilizer is a normal subgroup of index
  exactly `2` of the stabilizer of `w`.

All proved; none is a hypothesis. Proofs. Kernel: `ρ(g) = 1` on `W₁` forces `ρ(g) = 1` on
`W₂ ≅ W₁*`, and `ker ρ = {±1}` (Tau Ceti). Image: `⊆` is [Chevalley, III.3.2/III.4.5]
(`det₁ = χ₁²`); `⊇`: with a basis `a` of `W₁` and the dual family `b ⊆ W₂`, the transvections of
`W₁` lift to the Spin lifts `1 + c a_i b_j` of Eichler transvections, `diag(r², 1, …, 1)` lifts to
`s(r)` for `a₀, b₀` (`Sec2_4.lean`), `SL(W₁)` is generated by transvections (Mathlib's
`diagonal_transvection_induction'` and the Whitehead decomposition `sc_diag2n_decompose`), and
`A = (A D⁻¹) D`. The core statement `sc_exists_of_isSquare` keeps the lifts in any subgroup containing
them, which gives `sc_le_of_lifts` (used for the generation of `Spin(V)` in `Sec10.lean`).
Lemma 2: an element fixing `w` moves `u₁, u₂` to pure spinors `x, y` with `w = a x + b y`; after
transport to `u₁ ∝ 1`, `u₂ ∝ [pt_X]` ([Chevalley, §3.3, Lemma 1] and [III.1.4]), every `m_v x` lies
in degrees `1` and `2n − 1`, which forces `x ∈ span(1, [pt_X])` for `n ≥ 3` (`sc_repr_eq_zero_of_m`),
hence `x ∈ F 1 ∪ F [pt_X]` ([III.1.12]); so `g` fixes `u₁, u₂` or exchanges their lines
(`sc_stab_classify`), and an exchange forces `(u₁, u₂)_S = (-1)^n (u₁, u₂)_S` (invariance and
`(-1)^n`-symmetry of the Mukai pairing, [III.2.4]), impossible for `n` odd. For `n` even the
exchanging element (`sc_exists_swap`) comes from [Chevalley, §3.3, Lemma 1] for `(W₂, W₁)`, corrected
by an element of `Spin(V)_{ℓ₁,ℓ₂}` with prescribed character (`sc_exists_scalar`).

## `Sec10.lean`: [I, Prop. 3] and [I, Lemma 2] for `n = 3` (used in §10)

* `igusa_prop3_invariant`: `J(g x) = J(x)` for `g ∈ Spin(V_F)`, `x ∈ S⁺_F`. **Proved.**
  `Spin(V_F)` is generated by the root elements `1 + t e_i e_j`, the Levi elements `1 + c f_i e_j`,
  Igusa's elements `s(r)` for `f₁, e₁`, the Weyl elements `(f_a + e_a)(f_b + e_b)` and `-1`
  (`sc_closure_genSet_eq_top`, for every `n > 0`: Weyl elements move `g · 1` into the big cell, root
  elements move it to the line of `1` (`sc_bigcell`), the long Weyl element conjugates this to move
  `g · [pt_X]` to the line of `[pt_X]` fixing `1` (`sc_stepE`), and the stabilizer of both lines is
  generated by Levi and Igusa elements and `-1` (`sc_le_of_lifts`)). `J` is invariant under each
  generator by an explicit polynomial identity in the 32 coordinates (`sc_J_eqM` writes `J` in the
  bit-mask coordinates `sc_cm`; `sc_cm_ι_e`, `sc_cm_D_f` are the generator actions; 61 identities
  `sc_J_xp_ij`, `sc_J_wp_ij`, `sc_J_xl_ij`, `sc_J_hd`, each closed by `ring`/`field_simp`).
* `igusa_lemma2`: `ρ` maps the stabilizer of `1 + c [pt_X]` (`c ≠ 0`, over `ℂ`) onto the image of
  `e : SL(W₁) → SO(V_ℂ)`. **Proved** from `igusa_lemma2_stab_odd` and `igusa_lemma1_range`.
* `igusa_prop3_orbit_complex`: `J⁻¹(c) ⊆ S⁺_ℂ`, `c ≠ 0`, is one orbit. **Proved from**
  `igusa_prop3_normalForm_of_sq`, hence conditional on `IgusaProp3NormalForm`.
* `igusa_prop3_normalForm`: the case `F = K = ℚ(√-d)` used in Lemma 10.2.1. **Proved from**
  `igusa_prop3_normalForm_of_sq`, hence conditional on `IgusaProp3NormalForm`.
* `igusa_prop3_normalForm_of_sq` (if `s² = -J(w) ≠ 0` then `w ~ 1 + 2s [pt_X]` over `F`):
  **assumed**, the named hypothesis `IgusaProp3NormalForm`.
* `igusa_prop3_orbit_subfield` (`J⁻¹(d) ⊆ S⁺_F` one orbit for `F ⊆ ℂ`, `d ≠ 0`): **assumed**, the
  named hypothesis `IgusaProp3OrbitSubfield`.

### The two named hypotheses

The project owner chose (2026-10-04) to assume these two parts of [I, Prop. 3] rather than build the
classification they need. They are `Prop`-valued definitions, not axioms or instances: every result
that uses one takes it as an explicit argument, so a reader of the statement sees it.

* `IgusaProp3NormalForm`: over every field `F` (in `Type`) of characteristic zero, if `w ∈ S⁺_F`,
  `s ≠ 0` and `s² = -J(w)`, some `g ∈ Spin(V_F)` maps `w` to `1 + 2s [pt_X]`. This is the last
  paragraph of Igusa's proof. Its proof needs the classification of the generic `Spin(12)`-orbit on
  `S⁺`: every `w` with `J(w) ≠ 0` lies on a secant through two pure spinors with transversal
  maximal isotropic subspaces, defined over `F` when `-J(w)` is a square. Estimated at 1500–3000
  lines on top of the generation result above.
* `IgusaProp3OrbitSubfield`: for a subfield `F ⊆ ℂ` and `d ∈ F`, `d ≠ 0`, the level set `J⁻¹(d) ⊆ S⁺_F`
  is one `Spin(V_F)`-orbit. When `-d` is a square in `F` this follows from `IgusaProp3NormalForm`.
  Otherwise the stabilizer is the special unitary group of a hermitian form over `F(√-d)`, and the
  proof needs Galois cohomology (the injectivity of `H¹(F, SU(h)) → H¹(F, Spin(V))`, from Jacobson's
  theorem on hermitian forms), which Mathlib does not have.

Results of the paper that take a hypothesis (all in §10; the paper's main theorems do not use §10):

| Result | Lean | Hypothesis |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Lemma 10.1.1 (all three sentences) | `lemma10_1_1`, `lemma10_1_1_stabilizer`, `lemma10_1_1_rational` | `IgusaProp3NormalForm` |
| Remark 10.1.2(1), first sentence | `remark10_1_2_orbit` | `IgusaProp3OrbitSubfield` |
| Remark 10.1.2(2), rationality | `remark10_1_2_rational` | `IgusaProp3NormalForm` |
| Lemma 10.2.1 (both sentences, and the secant of its proof) | `lemma10_2_1`, `lemma10_2_1_centralizer`, `lemma10_2_1_secant` | `IgusaProp3NormalForm` |

The other results of §10 (Remark 10.1.2(1) second sentence and (2) first sentence, Examples 10.2.2,
10.2.3, the image of `η`) are unconditional.

Not stated, because no proof uses them: that the `Spin(V)`-invariant polynomials on `S⁺_ℚ` are the
polynomials in `J` (§10.1, l. 9642, context only), and the tangential-variety description of `V(J)`
([Abuaf, Rem. 2.1.1], l. 9643).
